key_people.name: Fred Dermarkar (Fred Dermarkar)
key_people.title: President and CEO
key_people.title_description: Leads AECL in its oversight role under the Government-owned, Contractor-operated model, ensuring government priorities are delivered safely and efficiently
key_people.description: Appointed President and CEO in 2021, reappointed to 2027. Nearly 40 years in the Canadian nuclear industry, previously President and CEO of the CANDU Owners Group. Holds a bachelor's degree in mechanical engineering from the University of Toronto.

key_people.name: James Burpee (James Burpee)
key_people.title: Chairperson of the Board of Directors
key_people.title_description: Chairs AECL's Board of Directors, providing strategic governance oversight
key_people.description: Serving as Chair since July 2019, term ending July 2029. Almost four decades in the electricity industry including senior roles at Ontario Hydro and Ontario Power Generation. Former President and CEO of the Canadian Electricity Association. Fellow of the Canadian Academy of Engineering.

key_people.name: Carmen Abela (Carmen Abela)
key_people.title: Board Member, Chair of Human Resources and Governance Committee
key_people.title_description: Oversees governance, risk management and human resources at the board level
key_people.description: Board member since 2017, term ending 2028. Founder and Managing Director of WindReach Consulting Services Inc. Chartered Director (C.Dir.) and Certified Internal Auditor (CIA).

key_people.name: Martha Tory (Martha Tory)
key_people.title: Board Member, Chair of Audit Committee
key_people.title_description: Chairs the Audit Committee overseeing financial reporting and compliance
key_people.description: Board member since 2016, term ending 2028. Retired audit partner from Ernst & Young LLP. Chartered Professional Accountant and Fellow of the Institute of Chartered Professional Accountants of Ontario.

key_people.name: Kamilia Sofia (Kamilia Sofia)
key_people.title: Board Member
key_people.title_description: Provides strategic oversight drawing on international executive experience in nuclear, aerospace and technology sectors
key_people.description: Board member since 2019, term ending 2027. Ph.D. in Nuclear Physics from McGill University. Former Executive Vice President of Rolls Royce Nuclear, CEO of Methanex Egypt. Named one of Canada's top 100 women in 2005.

departments.name: Science and Technology Department (Science and Technology)
departments.description: Oversees the Federal Nuclear Science and Technology Work Plan including health and biological applications, national security and emergency preparedness, new nuclear technologies, small modular reactors, medical isotopes, and commercial science and technology

departments.name: Radioactive Waste Management Department (Radioactive Waste Management)
departments.description: Manages the Government of Canada's radioactive waste responsibilities across multiple project sites including Chalk River Laboratories, Near Surface Disposal Facility, Port Hope Area Initiative, Whiteshell Laboratories, and decommissioning of legacy nuclear facilities

departments.name: Chalk River Revitalization Department (Chalk River Revitalization)
departments.description: Manages the revitalization of the Chalk River Laboratories site, transforming it into a world-class, state-of-the-art nuclear science and technology campus

recent_events.title: Nuclear Laboratory Partners of Canada Assumes Management of CNL
recent_events.description: AECL completed the contracting process for the management and operation of Canadian Nuclear Laboratories (CNL), with Nuclear Laboratory Partners of Canada Inc. (NLPC) officially taking responsibility. NLPC is a partnership of BWXT Government Group, Amentum Environment & Energy, and Kinectrics Inc., with Battelle Memorial Institute as key subcontractor. The transition was delayed from September due to an extended Competition Bureau review.
recent_events.impact: Major change in CNL management; NLPC led by Dennis Carr as President and CEO of CNL, overseeing 4,000+ employees across AECL sites

recent_events.title: AECL Establishes Centre for Fusion Energy in Pickering, Ontario
recent_events.description: AECL, in partnership with Canadian Nuclear Laboratories, Ontario Power Generation, and Stellarex, announced the establishment of a Centre for Fusion Energy. The federal government through AECL invested $33 million, Ontario committed $19.5 million, and Stellarex intends to contribute up to $39 million. The Centre aims to bolster Canada's growing fusion ecosystem and advance clean energy.
recent_events.impact: Significant investment in Canada's fusion energy research infrastructure, positioning Canada as a player in global fusion development

recent_events.title: AECL Selects NLPC as Preferred Bidder for CNL Management Contract
recent_events.description: AECL announced Nuclear Laboratory Partners of Canada Inc. (NLPC) as the Preferred Bidder for the contract to manage and operate Canadian Nuclear Laboratories beyond September 2025. NLPC is a BWXT-led joint venture with Amentum, Kinectrics, and Battelle, selected through a competitive procurement process that began in 2023.
recent_events.impact: Marks a major transition in the management of Canada's premier nuclear laboratory after the previous GoCo contract period

recent_events.title: AECL Joins Canadian Nuclear Isotope Council
recent_events.description: AECL formally partnered with the Canadian Nuclear Isotope Council (CNIC), leveraging AECL's foundational role in Canada's nuclear and isotopes industries. The partnership aims to grow Canada's isotope leadership, including production of molybdenum-99 and cobalt-60 for medical applications worldwide.
recent_events.impact: Strengthens Canada's position in global medical isotope supply chain; AECL is the world's largest supplier of cobalt-60 for cancer therapy

recent_events.title: AECL Federal Funding Decreases to $1.7 Billion for 2026-27
recent_events.description: According to the federal government's main spending estimates for 2026-27, AECL's funding will decrease to just over $1.7 billion, down from $1.94 billion in 2025-26. This marks the first funding decline in approximately twelve years.
recent_events.impact: Reduced federal funding may impact the pace of nuclear research programs and environmental remediation projects at AECL sites

core_business: 加拿大原子能有限公司（AECL）是加拿大联邦政府所属的皇家公司，成立于1952年，是加拿大最大的核科学与技术实验室。AECL的核心使命是通过核科学和技术为加拿大和世界提供能源、环境和经济利益。其主要业务涵盖四大领域：一是通过乔克河实验室（Chalk River Laboratories）等设施开展核科学与技术研究，包括联邦核科学技术工作计划中规定的健康与生物应用、国家安全与应急准备、新型核技术（含小型模块化反应堆SMR）以及医用同位素生产；二是代表加拿大政府管理放射性废物责任，包括多个历史核设施的去污退役和环境修复项目；三是拥有并管理CANDU重水反应堆技术的知识产权，该技术自1950年代起发展并已出口至印度、韩国、阿根廷、罗马尼亚和中国等国；四是通过政府所有、承包商运营（GoCo）模式，委托加拿大核实验室有限公司（CNL）运营其场地和资产，推进核创新、校园现代化和核聚变能源研究。AECL是全球最大的钼-99（用于医学诊断）和钴-60（用于癌症治疗）供应来源之一。2025年联邦拨款约19.4亿加元，拥有约3,500名员工。
apec_stance: 加拿大原子能有限公司作为加拿大联邦皇家公司，在亚太经合组织（APEC）框架下扮演着推动核能合作与技术输出的重要角色。AECL开发的CANDU重水反应堆技术已成功出口至多个APEC经济体，包括中国（秦山三期核电站）、韩国（月城核电站2/3/4号机组）等。在APEC强调清洁能源转型和应对气候变化的背景下，AECL通过小型模块化反应堆（SMR）技术、医用同位素供应和核聚变能源研究等前沿领域，积极推动加拿大与APEC成员经济体在核能和平利用方面的合作。加拿大作为核能技术输出国，通过AECL的技术优势和国际合作，支持APEC区域内安全、可持续的核能发展。AECL也是世界核协会（WNA）成员，在国际核能治理标准制定中发挥作用。
